result.target_summary: Elevated inflation and interest rates have negatively impacted investment securities, deposits, loan demand, and funding costs, although they have generally boosted net interest income. comparisons.peer_topic: Interest Rate Risk and Net Interest Income Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi's net interest income may decline if benchmark interest rates drop or if the yield curve flattens or inverts, as Citi typically pays on shorter-term deposits while earning on longer-term loans; Corporate Treasury utilizes tools to manage this interest rate risk.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C disclose that net interest income is sensitive to interest rate levels, with both noting that lower rates or a flat/inverted yield curve could reduce NII. BAC states that future rate cuts would typically result in lower revenue through lower net interest income (bac_2024_1A_P005_S009). Similarly, Citi notes that a decline in interest rates would generally result in lower overall net interest income (c_2024_1A_P005_S002) and that NII could be adversely affected by a flattening or inversion of the yield curve (c_2024_1A_P005_S003). Both also acknowledge that elevated rates have generally boosted NII but pose downside risks if rates drop.

sentences.text: Any future change in monetary policy by the Federal Reserve, in an effort to stimulate the economy or otherwise, resulting in lower interest rates would typically result in lower revenue through lower net interest income, which could adversely affect our results of operations.
Monetary policy has contributed to and may continue to result in elevated market interest rates and a flat and/or inverted yield curve.

A decline in interest rates would generally be expected to result in lower overall net interest income for Citi, although Corporate Treasury has various tools to manage Citi's total interest rate risk position (see "Managing Global Risk- Market Risk-Market Risk of Non-Trading Portfolios" below).

In addition, Citi's net interest income could be adversely affected due to a flattening (a lower spread between shorter-term versus longer-term interest rates) or inversion (shorter-term interest rates exceeding longer-term interest rates) of the interest rate yield curve, as Citi typically pays interest on deposits based on shorter-term interest rates and earns money on loans based on longer-term interest rates.

comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of Declining Asset Values, Market Volatility, and Interest Rates on Financial Performance
comparisons.peer_summary: Declining asset values, driven by market volatility, interest rate increases, and inflation, adversely affect the company's financial results through multiple channels: net long positions incur mark-to-market losses that are difficult to hedge; exchange-based market-making faces liquidity needs and increased capital requirements (RWAs) in volatile markets; collateral value declines trigger margin calls and increase funding costs; asset-based management and incentive fees decline as client assets drop or shift to lower-fee products; and investment banking revenues suffer from reduced transaction volumes due to lack of investor confidence. Higher interest rates also increase borrowing costs and can reduce net interest income.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS highlight that central bank responses to inflation have led to higher market interest rates and inflationary pressures, which adversely affect financial markets. BAC notes that elevated inflation and interest rates have adversely impacted financial markets and macroeconomic conditions (bac_2024_1A_P004_S002). GS similarly states that central bank responses to inflationary pressures resulted in higher market interest rates, contributing to lower activity levels and adversely affecting equity and debt investments (gs_2024_1A_P038_S003). Both identify monetary policy and inflation as key drivers of current market conditions.

sentences.text: Elevated inflation and interest rate levels, monetary tightening by central banks, and geopolitical developments, including the Russia/Ukraine conflict and the conflicts in the Middle East, have adversely impacted and could continue to adversely impact financial markets and macroeconomic conditions, as well as result in additional market volatility and disruptions and recessionary risk.

Central bank responses to inflationary pressures in recent years have also resulted in higher market interest rates, which, in turn, have contributed to lower activity levels across financial markets, in particular for debt underwriting transactions and mortgage originations, and resulted in lower values for certain financial assets which have adversely affected our equity and debt investments.

comparisons.peer_summary: High interest rates can lead to fewer loan originations, deposit losses, and AFS security losses, while low rates can compress net interest margins and reduce the value of mortgage servicing rights, both adversely affecting earnings, liquidity, and capital.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM analyze the dual impact of interest rates on their business: higher rates can boost net interest income but also bring risks such as deposit losses or credit stress. BAC notes that elevated rates have generally boosted net interest income but could result in lower revenue if rates drop, while also raising uncertainty (bac_2024_1A_P005_S004, bac_2024_1A_P005_S009). JPM explicitly states that when interest rates are high, it can generally be expected to earn higher net interest income, but high rates can also lead to deposit losses, fewer loan originations, and negatively affect payment performance on variable-rate loans (jpm_2024_1A_P065_S001, jpm_2024_1A_P065_S005, jpm_2024_1A_P066_S002).

comparisons.peer_topic: Interest Rate Sensitivity and Net Interest Income
comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income is sensitive to interest rate changes, with rate levels and pace impacting client cash allocation, deposit mix, and loan demand, which may adversely affect operations.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS disclose that net interest income is sensitive to interest rate changes, with higher rates generally leading to higher NII and lower rates leading to lower NII. BAC states that any future change resulting in lower interest rates would typically result in lower revenue through lower net interest income (bac_2024_1A_P005_S009). MS explicitly states that its net interest income is sensitive to changes in interest rates, generally resulting in higher NII in higher scenarios and lower NII in lower scenarios (ms_2024_1A_P011_S001). Both link this sensitivity to the broader impact on results of operations.

sentences.text: Any future change in monetary policy by the Federal Reserve, in an effort to stimulate the economy or otherwise, resulting in lower interest rates would typically result in lower revenue through lower net interest income, which could adversely affect our results of operations.

Our net interest income is sensitive to changes in interest rates, generally resulting in higher net interest income in higher interest rate scenarios and lower net interest income in lower interest rate scenarios.
